welcomePage.title: Get started
welcomePage.description: Network IDS takes the alerts, flows and protocol logs of Suricata sensors that see a copy of your traffic, and gives every sensor your local rules and suppressions.
welcomePage.step1: Put Suricata on a host that sees a copy of the traffic: a mirror (SPAN) port or a tap.
welcomePage.step2: Add a sensor here. You get a one-time token and the command that starts network-ids-agent next to Suricata.
welcomePage.step3: Point Suricata at the agent's rules and threshold files, as Setup shows, and turn on its command socket.
welcomePage.step4: Alerts, flows and protocol logs show here within seconds; write local rules and suppressions under Rules.

alertsPage.title: Alerts
alertsPage.description: Signatures that matched traffic on your sensors, with the flow around each. Network IDS detects; it does not block.
alertsPage.perHourDetail: By severity, the last 24 hours, without suppressed ones.
alertsPage.talkersDetail: Sources by bytes in their flows, 24 h.
alertsPage.noFlows: No flows yet. Suricata writes a flow when it ends or times out.
alertsPage.select: Select an alert to see its flow, protocol logs and EVE event
alertsPage.flowLater: The flow shows once Suricata ends it.
alertsPage.noRecords: No protocol logs on this flow.

suppress.title: Suppress a signature
suppress.description: Known-good traffic that should not alert.
suppress.reasonHint: Why this traffic is known to be good, such as: the build runner fetches with curl.

flowsPage.title: Flows
flowsPage.description: Every connection Suricata ended, searchable by its fields: who talked to whom, how long and how much.
flowsPage.unansweredHelp: Nothing came back: scans and blocked ports
flowsPage.stateHelp: How Suricata saw the flow end: new (no answer), established, closed or bypassed.
flowsPage.select: Select a flow to see its protocol logs and alerts

protocolsPage.title: Protocols
protocolsPage.description: DNS, HTTP, TLS and SSH as Suricata logged them. Encrypted traffic shows its metadata, not its content.
protocolsPage.none: Nothing logged for this protocol in the last 24 hours

rulesPage.title: Rules
rulesPage.description: Local rules and suppressions, given to every sensor. Rulesets such as ET Open stay with suricata-update on each sensor.
rulesPage.outdated_one: {{count}} sensor has not written the current rules yet
rulesPage.outdated_other: {{count}} sensors have not written the current rules yet
rulesPage.outdatedDetail: Each agent writes them at its next call and reloads Suricata. A sensor that is offline writes them when it is back.
rulesPage.writeDetail: Suricata syntax: alert or pass, SIDs from 9,000,000 to 9,999,999. Lua, datasets and reputation files are not sent.
rulesPage.saved: Saved sid {{sid}}: every sensor writes it at its next call
rulesPage.suppressionsDetail: Known-good traffic that should not alert.
rulesPage.author: Written by
rulesPage.rulesetsDetail: Keep ET Open and other rulesets with suricata-update on each sensor, as you do now; Rules loaded counts them all. Choosing rulesets here is planned.

sensorsPage.title: Sensors
sensorsPage.description: Where Suricata listens, what it sees and what it drops. Above 1% dropped, rules miss traffic.
sensorsPage.addDetail: One Suricata that sees a copy of the traffic, with network-ids-agent next to it.
sensorsPage.name: Name
sensorsPage.nameHint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, such as nids-core-01.
sensorsPage.whereHint: Such as: Frankfurt DC, core switch SPAN.
sensorsPage.enrolDetail: On the sensor host, with this one-time token. It works once, until {{when}}, and is not shown again.
sensorsPage.noneDetail: Add one, then start its agent next to Suricata.
sensorsPage.waiting: Waiting for its agent to enrol with the token.
sensorsPage.dropRate: Packet drop rate for {{name}}, last 24 hours
sensorsPage.configError: The agent could not write or reload the rules
sensorsPage.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}} with every alert, flow and log it sent?
sensorsPage.dropsDetail: Suricata cannot keep up: add capture workers, give it more CPU, or move the sensor to a larger host.

setupPage.title: Setup
setupPage.description: How a sensor is put together: Suricata on a copy of the traffic, and network-ids-agent next to it.
setupPage.suricataDetail: Write EVE JSON with these event types, load the agent's rules and threshold files, and open the command socket so the agent can reload rules.
setupPage.agentDetail: On the same host, with Suricata's log directory read-only and the directory of the agent's files writable. Add the sensor under Sensors for its token.
setupPage.how1: It reads eve.json from where it stopped, follows it across rotation, and sends alerts, flows, protocol logs and counters. Packet payloads stay on the sensor.
setupPage.how2: It asks for the local rules and suppressions, checks every line again, writes openasy.rules and threshold.config, and asks Suricata to reload rules. It runs no command it is sent.
setupPage.how3: It connects out and never listens for Network IDS. It enrols once with the token, then uses its own secret, sealed with its own key.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Network IDS.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Network IDS, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also write local rules and suppressions; admins also add sensors, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
